subject: VPC pricing & platform fee split — pilot concession and support tiers
messages:
From: Tom Bradley <t.bradley@mediascope.com>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 20 May 2027 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: VPC pricing questions and pilot concession request

Hi Mateo,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — the latency numbers look very promising. Procurement and our infra team asked me to get a clearer picture of commercial options for a private VPC deployment. A few items they want explicitly called out:

- How the platform fee is amortized across pilots vs committed capacity (can you provide an example invoice cadence?)
- Support tiers and response SLAs for on-prem/VPC (SRE retainer options, on-call hours)
- Any one-time implementation credits or pilot discounts you’d be willing to extend for a 6-month pilot (we’d like to validate inference at ~500 tpm and 100 concurrent sessions)
- A draft SOW we can push through legal (redlines likely) and approximate lead times to get a pilot up and running

Can you send a concise set of options + a rough price sheet that separates platform fee, per-node license, and SRE retainer? I attached our procurement template (Procurement_Scope_MediaScope.xlsx) for reference.

Best,
Tom
Tom Bradley
Head of Platform Ops, MediaScope
procurement@mediascope.com

From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.com>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 21 May 2027 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: VPC pricing questions and pilot concession request

Hi Tom — thanks for the clear ask and the template. I put together three packaging options (attached) that separate platform fee, node licensing, and support so your procurement can map line items to your cost center:

1) Pilot (6 months):
   - One-off setup fee: $15k (covers initial onboarding, infra runbook, and deployment).
   - Platform fee: 60% of list for first 6 months (pilot concession), then reverts to full rate unless a commit is signed.
   - Node license: metered by instance (per-GPU / per-node).
   - SRE retainer: optional $8k/mo for 24x7 on-call with 2hr response; lower tiers available.

2) Committed (12 months):
   - Platform fee amortized monthly over the term (example included).
   - 20% discount on platform fee with 12mo committed baseline.
   - Priority scheduling and quarterly performance review.

3) Enterprise (multi-site, custom):
   - Enterprise platform fee with volume tiers and SRE retainer bundled.
   - Can include a portion of the platform fee as a capitalized prepay if you prefer capex treatment.

Ask: can you confirm the expected average token throughput and whether the 100 concurrent sessions estimate is steady or bursty? That will materially affect node count and SRE coverage.

Attached: redwood_privdeploy_pricing_options.xlsx (pricing tabs + example invoice cadence). Also happy to hop on a 30m call with procurement/legal to walk through the SOW.

Thanks,
Mateo Alvarez
Account Executive — Redwood Inference
mateo.alvarez@redwood.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Cc: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 22 May 2027 14:30:00 -0700
Subject: Internal: proposed concession math and margin impact

Folks — quick internal note on the numbers (I ran the model against their stated 500 tpm / ~100 concurrency). High level:

- Pilot concession: 40% off platform fee for first 6 months (we're already giving 60% in the customer-facing note; propose we move to 40% to protect gross margin). Cap pilot to 6 months or 100k generated tokens, whichever comes first.
- Committed option: 20% platform fee discount on a 12mo commit; require a minimum committed baseline (e.g., 4 reserved nodes).
- SRE retainer: offer two tiers — Basic (business hours, 4hr response, $4k/mo) and Premium (24x7, 2hr response, $8k/mo). Suggest we include one complimentary health-check during pilot.
- Implementation credit: $10k credit toward setup if they convert to committed within 90 days of pilot end.

We should flag legal on the SOW language around liability for on-prem incident remediation (Alex, can you please pre-seed the SOW with the standard ops carveouts?). Also note: if they push for SOC2 evidence in procurement, we can point them to the hosted SOC2 artifact but will not include any additional on-prem SOC2 work in the concession.

If OK, I’ll update the pricing sheet and send to Tom Monday morning.

—Marissa
Director, Commercials — Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com

Hi Tom — looping back with an updated, procurement-friendly proposal and a draft SOW attached.

Per the internal review we can offer the following (summary):
- Pilot: 40% off platform fee for the first 6 months, capped at 100k tokens or 6 months. One complimentary health-check.
- Node licensing: metered; example costs shown for the 4-node baseline that maps to your 500 tpm estimate.
- SRE retainer options: Basic $4k/mo (business hours), Premium $8k/mo (24x7).
- Implementation credit: $10k credit if you convert to a 12mo committed plan within 90 days of pilot completion.

Attached is Mediascope_SOW_draft.docx (contains milestone-based deliverables, responsibilities, and a sample invoice cadence). Once your legal team sends redlines we’ll convert to a DocuSign envelope (link below). Please also confirm procurement timeline and the PO billing contact so we can prep the invoice.

> - Please confirm whether the 100 concurrent sessions are steady or bursty.

If steady, our baseline above is correct; if bursty we'll size additional burst capacity and provide a separate burst billing line.

DocuSign link (provisional): https://docusign.com/envelopes/ABC-123-REDWOOD-MS

- We agree to the 40% platform fee concession for the 6-month pilot, capped as you described.
- 100 concurrent sessions are expected to be steady during peak business hours (09:00–18:00 PT); we’ll provide a traffic profile before contract execution.
- We’ll sign the SOW pending two small legal redlines (terms around indemnity and an SLA uptime clarification). Expect redlines from legal tomorrow.
